item.title: Apple plans to open Siri to rival AI chatbots in iOS 27
item.description: Apple is planning to open Siri to rival artificial intelligence services, ending OpenAI's exclusive chatbot partnership with the iPhone maker and transforming the device into a broader AI platform, Bloomberg reported on Thursday. The move will allow companies like Google and Anthropic to integrate their chatbots directly with Siri in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27.

item.title: Fossil ape found in Egypt challenges East Africa origin theory
item.description:
A newly identified fossil ape unearthed in northern Egypt is prompting scientists to reconsider where modern apes — including humans — first evolved. The species, named Masripithecus moghraensis, lived roughly 17 to 18 million years ago and represents the first definitive fossil ape ever found in North Africa, according to a study published Thursday in the journal Science.

An international team from Egypt's Mansoura University Vertebrate Paleontology Center and the University of Southern California recovered the fossils — a partial lower jaw and several teeth — from the Wadi Moghra site in northern Egypt during fieldwork in 2023 and 2024.

item.title: Study finds AI chatbots affirm users 49% more than humans do
item.description: A new study published Thursday in the journal Science found that leading AI chatbots are so prone to flattering their users that they routinely dispense bad advice, damage relationships, and reinforce harmful behaviors. The research, led by Stanford University scientists, tested 11 major AI systems and found they all exhibited varying degrees of sycophancy — overly agreeable behavior that users, paradoxically, tend to prefer.

item.title: Trump extends pause on Iran energy strikes to April 6
item.description:
President Donald Trump on Thursday announced he would extend a halt on U.S. military strikes targeting Iran's energy infrastructure by 10 days, pushing the deadline to April 6 as the White House signaled both diplomatic openness and a readiness to escalate.

"As per Iranian Government request I am pausing the period of Energy Plant destruction by 10 Days to Monday, April 6, 2026, at 8 P.M., Eastern Time," Trump wrote on Truth Social, according to CNBC. He added that "talks are ongoing and they are going very well," pushing back against what he called "erroneous statements" from the media.

item.title: US senators introduce bill to sanction Hungary over Ukraine aid blockade
item.description:
A bipartisan group of US senators has introduced legislation that would impose financial sanctions and visa bans on Hungarian government officials, escalating Washington's response to Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's continued obstruction of a €90 billion European Union loan to Ukraine. The bill, called the Block Putin Act, was put forward by Senators Jeanne Shaheen, a Democrat from New Hampshire, and Thom Tillis, a Republican from North Carolina, according to the Financial Times.

The move comes as Orbán, facing his toughest re-election fight in 16 years ahead of April 12 parliamentary elections, has deepened an anti-Ukraine campaign that now includes allegations of Ukrainian intelligence interference in Hungarian domestic politics.

item.title: Iran offers Spain Hormuz access in first such EU overture
item.description:
The Iranian embassy in Spain announced on Thursday that Tehran would be "receptive to any request coming from Madrid" related to the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first such overture to a European Union nation since Iran began restricting traffic through the vital waterway nearly a month ago.

The embassy's post on X cited Spain's "commitment to international law" as the basis for the gesture. The announcement followed a note from Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs to the United Nations, seen by Reuters on Tuesday, stating that "non-hostile vessels" could transit the strait if they coordinated with Iranian authorities.

item.title: Pentagon confirms first use of drone boats in Iran conflict
item.description:
The United States has deployed uncrewed drone speedboats for patrol missions as part of its military operations against Iran, the Pentagon confirmed on Thursday, marking the first time Washington has used such vessels in an active conflict.

The disclosure, first reported by Reuters, reveals that the Global Autonomous Reconnaissance Craft, or GARC — built by Maryland-based BlackSea Technologies — has been conducting maritime patrols in support of Operation Epic Fury, the U.S.-led campaign launched against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: Trump extends Iran strike deadline to April 6 as markets tumble, oil tops $100
item.description: The nearly month-old war in Iran sent fresh shockwaves through the global economy on Thursday as the OECD warned that U.S. inflation will reach 4.2% this year, Wall Street suffered another steep selloff, and oil prices pushed back above $100 a barrel — all consequences of Iran's ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: UK pledges £100M more for Ukraine's air defenses
item.description: Britain announced an additional £100 million in air defence support for Ukraine, according to Reuters, bringing the country's total contribution to Ukrainian air defences to roughly £600 million over the past two months. The pledge underscores London's position as one of Kyiv's most steadfast military backers as Russia's aerial campaign against Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure continues into the conflict's fifth year.

item.title: Brown-Forman and Pernod Ricard confirm merger talks
item.description:
Pernod Ricard and Brown-Forman, two of the world's largest spirits companies, confirmed on Thursday that they are engaged in discussions over a potential combination that would reshape the global liquor landscape. The talks, first reported by Bloomberg on March 26, were described by both companies as a "merger of equals."

In a statement issued via Business Wire, Brown-Forman said the potential partnership would create "a global spirits leader with enhanced scale, a powerful brand portfolio, and a balanced geographic footprint, all anchored by two iconic families." Pernod Ricard issued a near-identical statement, emphasizing that "operational synergies would be significant."

item.title: Houthi leader signals readiness to join Iran war against US and Israel
item.description:
Abdul-Malik al-Houthi, leader of Yemen's Ansarallah movement, warned on Thursday of a "military response" should the ongoing war between Iran and the United States and Israel require it, in his most direct signal yet that the group may open a new front in the nearly month-old conflict.

"As the people of Yemen, we repay loyalty with loyalty," al-Houthi said in a speech broadcast on the group's Al-Masirah channel. "Any development in the battle that requires a military response, we will promptly undertake it... just as we did in previous rounds."

item.title: Iran opens Hormuz to 5 'friendly' nations as oil tops $100
item.description:
The S&P 500 fell 1.7% on Thursday — its worst single-day drop since the U.S.-Israel war on Iran began in late February — as crude oil prices surged past $105 a barrel and Iran further consolidated control over the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway through which roughly one-fifth of the world's oil supply flows.

Brent crude settled at $101.89 on Wednesday before jumping again Thursday morning, climbing nearly 5% as Iran rejected a U.S. ceasefire proposal delivered via Pakistan and denied that direct talks with Washington were underway. The price of oil has risen roughly 55% since the conflict began on February 28.

item.title: Anthropic discusses Q4 2026 IPO that could raise over $60B
item.description:
Anthropic executives have discussed going public as soon as the fourth quarter of 2026, with investment bankers competing for the mandate expecting the AI startup to raise more than $60 billion in its initial public offering, according to a report from The Information published on Thursday. If realized, the listing would rank among the largest IPOs in history and mark a defining moment for the AI industry's transition from private fundraising to public markets.

The potential offering comes as rival OpenAI is also targeting a fourth-quarter IPO, setting up a high-stakes race between the two leading AI companies for investor attention. The Wall Street Journal reported in January that OpenAI was preparing its own blockbuster debut, with the ChatGPT maker aiming for a valuation approaching $1 trillion.

item.title: S&P 500 posts worst day since Iran war began as oil tops $100
item.description:
Wall Street suffered its worst day since the war with Iran began on Thursday as Iran tightened its grip on the Strait of Hormuz, sending oil prices sharply higher and dashing hopes for a swift diplomatic resolution to the nearly month-long conflict. The S&P 500 slumped 1.7%, putting it on track for a fifth consecutive losing week, while Brent crude settled at $101.89 per barrel, up 4.8% on the day, according to the Associated Press.

The selloff came after Iran rejected a 15-point U.S. ceasefire proposal delivered via Pakistan and issued its own demands, including recognition of its sovereign control over the strait — a condition the White House called a nonstarter. President Donald Trump, who had previously threatened to strike Iran's power plants if the waterway was not reopened, extended his deadline to April 6, saying the delay came "at the request of Iran".

item.title: Experts warn Iran war's environmental toll could persist for decades
item.description: Nearly a month into the conflict that began on February 28 with U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran under "Operation Epic Fury," environmental scientists are raising alarms about a growing ecological catastrophe across the Middle East. A toxic combination of chemicals, heavy metals, and pollutants from burning oil facilities, sunken ships, and destroyed infrastructure now threatens the region's air, water, and soil for decades to come, according to experts and monitoring groups.

item.title: China's SMIC sent chipmaking tools to Iran's military, US officials say
item.description:
SMIC, China's largest chipmaker, has supplied semiconductor manufacturing equipment to Iran's military, two senior Trump administration officials said on Thursday, a disclosure that could deepen tensions between Washington and Beijing amid the month-old U.S.-Israeli war with Iran.

The officials, speaking to Reuters on condition of anonymity, said SMIC began shipping the tools to Iran roughly a year ago and that "we have no reason to believe that any of this has stopped". The collaboration "almost certainly included technical training on SMIC's semiconductor technology," one of the officials added.

item.title: Iranian hardliners push for nuclear weapon as war escalates
item.description:
The war between the United States, Israel, and Iran has entered dangerous nuclear territory, with both sides striking near or at each other's most sensitive atomic installations and international monitors warning of a potential radiological catastrophe.

On March 24, a projectile struck the premises of Iran's Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant for the second time since hostilities began on February 28, prompting IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi to reiterate his call for "maximum restraint to avoid nuclear safety risks during the ongoing conflict". The first strike near Bushehr on March 17 hit a structure just 350 meters from the operating reactor, destroying it, according to the IAEA. Iran reported no damage to the reactor itself or injuries to staff in either incident, though Russia's Rosatom has begun evacuating personnel from the site it helped build.

item.title: US has lost at least 16 aircraft in Iran war as losses mount
item.description: Nearly a month into Operation Epic Fury, the United States has lost at least 16 military aircraft — and possibly as many as 20 — in its air campaign against Iran, according to reporting from Air & Space Forces Magazine and multiple defense outlets. The toll includes an F-35A stealth fighter damaged by Iranian ground fire on March 19, marking the first time the advanced jet has been struck by enemy fire in its operational history.

item.title: Iran claims 1 million fighters ready for US ground invasion
item.description: Iran's state-run media declared Thursday that more than one million fighters have been organized for ground combat against American forces, as speculation intensifies over a potential US assault on Iran's southern coast and the strategically vital Kharg Island. The claim, reported by the IRGC-affiliated Tasnim News Agency, came alongside a warning that any US attempt to seize the Strait of Hormuz would amount to "suicide."

item.title: Iran war chokes global fertilizer supply as planting season begins
item.description: Nearly a month into the U.S.-Israel military campaign against Iran, the near-total closure of the Strait of Hormuz is choking off roughly one-third of the world's seaborne fertilizer trade, sending prices surging and raising alarms about a looming food crisis just as the Northern Hemisphere's planting season begins.
